title: Elastic prefix caching and adaptive page hedging for operator dashboard query API
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Operator and admin dashboards are seeing high p95/p99 tail latency for paginated queries when tenants trigger large ad-hoc filters and long time-window rollups. Existing cursor pagination hits many shards and either returns very small pages (many round trips) or large pages (heavy CPU/memory). This ticket proposes two coordinated mitigations: 1) elastic prefix caching — maintain compact, tenant-scoped prefix summaries and small per-shard bloom/range filters to answer early-page requests from cache for common prefixes; 2) adaptive page hedging — a request orchestration layer that issues parallel hedged queries with different page-size/shard-priority profiles and picks the fastest complete page, reducing tail latency without always increasing average cost.

Goals and success criteria:
- Reduce dashboard query p95 latency by >= 30% for filtered/time-windowed operator queries.
- Keep p50 roughly equal (<10% regression) and limit additional token/compute cost to <15% on average for hedged flows.
- No customer-visible correctness regressions (ordering/stability of cursors preserved), and GC/memory pressure stays within current operational limits.

Design overview:
- Elastic prefix caching: build a compact prefix cache that stores summarized ordered keys + top-K token counts for the first N rows per tenant-shard. Summaries are capped and evicted with LRU+frequency heuristics. Each cache entry includes a small bloom filter to quickly rule out shard candidates for a given filter predicate. Cache keys use normalized query signatures (time-range bucket, normalized filters, projection set) to maximize reuse across UI interactions.
- Adaptive page hedging: when a dashboard route requests pages, the router consults estimates from the prefix cache and the recent latency model (per-tenant, per-shard) to decide whether to issue a single canonical request or N hedged requests in parallel. Hedged strategies include: (a) narrow fast-first: small page size targeted at hot shards first; (b) wide single-shot: larger page that touches more shards but fewer round trips; (c) cached-probe: hit cache-only read path to attempt a cheap short-circuit. The router reconciles results by deterministic merge rules and issues stable next-cursor tokens.

Indexing and compatibility:
- Requires small index metadata additions to per-shard stores (prefix summaries + bloom bitset). We will add a compact on-disk companion file per shard with versioned format (backwards compatible fallbacks use full scan if companion missing).
- No changes to API surface for clients; feature gated at server-side with rollout flags.

Trade-offs and considerations:
- Memory vs CPU: prefix cache increases memory pressure; we will cap tenant memory and use a circuit-breaker to disable cache under pressure. Hedging increases upstream load—we will limit hedging concurrency per-tenant and back off under elevated infra utilization.
- Staleness: prefix summaries are eventually consistent with writes; queries requiring strict point-in-time semantics will bypass cache. We will expose a telemetry label when cached reads are used.
- Observability: instrument cache hit/miss, hedged vs single-path counts, cost delta, and p50/p95 latencies per tenant.

Rollout plan:
1) Implement storage companion and prefix cache read-path behind feature flag; unit + integration tests. (canary=single internal tenant)
2) Add adaptive hedging router behind separate flag and run canaries at 5% of internal traffic.
3) Expand to a small set of friendly customers and monitor cost + latencies for 2 weeks.
4) Gradual ramp to 100% with runtime limits and automatic disable if GC/CPU alarms fire.

Testing and benchmarks:
- Microbenchmarks: synthetic query shapes covering top-k, high-cardinality filters, and wide time windows. Expect single-path p95 420ms -> 280ms for canary.
- End-to-end: use production-like replay (observability replay job) to estimate cost delta; include mitigations if cost > 15%.

Operational runbooks:
- Feature flag quick-disable via console for prefix cache and hedging.
- Monitoring alerts: cache eviction rate > 10k/min, hedged request ratio > 20%, p95 latency regression > 10% vs baseline.
